title: The Christmas gathering

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: I have brought the canapés we planned. Has everyone arrived?

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: Yes. Taylor, Evan, Sara, Denali and Maria are here.

dialogue.speaker: Evan
dialogue.text: I have finally finished my financial report, so I can relax.

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: We have prepared a salad. Where should we put it?

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.text: I have never tried these canapés before. They look wonderful.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.text: Let’s take a picture before we sit down. We have made a great team.

reading: The Christmas gathering planned in PRACTICAL now takes place. Clarice has brought canapés, and Taylor’s family has prepared a salad. Ethan welcomes Taylor, Evan, Sara, Denali and Maria. Evan has finished a financial report; he is a financial analyst, not a hospital employee. The friends have shared the preparation as agreed. Sara suggests a group photograph before the meal. The gathering celebrates both the holiday and the friendships that have developed.

questions.prompt: What does Sara suggest before the meal?

task: Write four statements about what the friends have already done and two questions about what they have not done yet.

title: A confident first step

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.text: I had avoided swimming lessons because I felt nervous in the water.

dialogue.speaker: Caleb
dialogue.text: Thank you for telling me. You can decide what you feel ready to try.

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.text: I had spoken to the instructor before I booked this beginner session.

dialogue.speaker: Caleb
dialogue.text: That was a good idea. I can wait here while you have your lesson.

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.text: I would like that. Today I only want to practice in the shallow end.

dialogue.speaker: Caleb
dialogue.text: Take your time. We can talk afterward.

reading: In January, Maria attends a beginner lesson at a heated indoor pool. She had avoided swimming because she felt nervous. Before booking, she had spoken to the instructor about her concerns. Caleb accompanies her and respects her decision to begin in the shallow end. The qualified instructor leads the lesson. Maria chooses her own pace, and Caleb waits nearby. This is a small, deliberate step toward a goal she has wanted to pursue.

questions.prompt: When does the lesson take place?
Whom had Maria spoken to before booking?
Where does she want to begin?

task: Describe two events that happened before Maria arrived. Use past perfect for the earlier event and past simple for the later event.

title: A Sunday plan

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: Good morning! Would you like to meet at nine thirty?

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: Yes. I have already had breakfast, but I would love a walk.

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: I need to send two messages first. I will have finished them by nine.

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: I will have packed a small picnic by the time you arrive.

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: Perfect. We will have reached the park before it gets busy.

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: And by noon, we will have enjoyed a peaceful morning together.

reading: On the Sunday after Maria’s lesson, Ethan calls Clarice. They agree to meet at nine thirty. Clarice has already eaten breakfast, so they choose a walk and a small picnic. Ethan expects to have finished his messages by nine. Clarice will have packed the picnic before he arrives. They plan to reach the park before it becomes busy and to spend a quiet morning together. The future perfect describes what will be complete by a future time.

questions.prompt: What will Ethan have finished by nine?

task: Write three predictions using will have + past participle and a deadline introduced by by or by the time.

title: A misunderstanding at dinner

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: We are late. I thought Sara was still getting ready.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.text: I was waiting by the door. You might not have heard me call.

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: You are right. I should have checked before blaming you.

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: We were wondering what had happened. You could have sent a message.

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: I am sorry. Next time, we will agree on a meeting time and send an update.

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: You are here now. Let’s enjoy dinner together.

reading: Later in January, Taylor and Sara arrive late for dinner with Clarice and Ethan. Taylor had assumed Sara was still getting ready, but Sara had been waiting by the door. Taylor realizes she should have checked before blaming her. Clarice says they could have sent a message. The family agrees to communicate more clearly next time. No one is being introduced for the first time: these friends already know one another.
task: Use should have, could have and might have to reflect on the misunderstanding. Distinguish a suggestion from a possibility.

title: A new chapter

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: If you are ready for another adventure together, I have a question.

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: You look nervous. What is it?

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: Will you marry me?

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: Yes! I would love to. If we plan carefully, we can celebrate with our friends.

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: How about September nineteenth?

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: That gives us time. If I had unlimited time, I would design everything myself, but we can ask for help.

reading: In February, Ethan proposes to Clarice, and she accepts. They choose September nineteenth for their wedding. They want their friends to be part of the celebration, and they know that planning will take time. Clarice says that she would design everything herself if she had unlimited time. In reality, they will share the work and ask for help. This is their engagement; the wedding has not happened yet.

questions.prompt: How will they manage the preparations?

task: Write a general planning rule, a realistic future possibility and an imaginary situation. Label the conditional type.

title: The missing invitation

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.text: I heard about the invitations, but mine has not arrived. Did I misunderstand something?

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: You are invited, of course. I may have used your old address.

dialogue.speaker: Denali
dialogue.text: We moved last year. Let’s check the list together.

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: Here is the mistake. If I had checked the address, the invitation would have reached you.

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.text: If I had asked sooner, I would not have worried so much.

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: I am glad we talked. I will send the corrected invitation today.

reading: In March, Maria worries because her wedding invitation has not arrived. She asks Clarice directly instead of assuming she was excluded. Clarice and Denali check the guest list and discover an old address. Clarice apologizes and sends a corrected invitation. Maria realizes that asking sooner would have saved her some worry. The mistake is administrative, not a change in their friendship. Both women describe how the past might have been different.

questions.prompt: Why did the invitation not arrive?

task: Write two third conditional sentences about the address mistake. Keep the imagined past separate from what really happened.

title: A birthday worth celebrating

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.text: My birthday dinner was interrupted by an uncomfortable argument with my date.

dialogue.speaker: Denali
dialogue.text: I am sorry. You deserve to be treated with respect.

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.text: I left early. A taxi was called by the restaurant staff, and I came home.

dialogue.speaker: Denali
dialogue.text: Would you like a quiet celebration here instead?

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.text: Yes. I turn twenty-nine today, and I want to spend the evening with a friend.

dialogue.speaker: Denali
dialogue.text: Then tea and cake it is. The candles have already been set out.

reading: In August, Maria turns twenty-nine. Her birthday dinner with a date is interrupted by an argument, and she decides to leave. A taxi is called by the restaurant staff. At home, Denali listens without judging and offers tea and cake. The candles have already been set out. Maria chooses a calm celebration with her roommate. The episode uses passive forms to describe events while keeping Maria’s decisions and boundaries clear.

questions.prompt: Who celebrates with Maria at home?

task: Rewrite three active sentences from the episode in the passive. Keep the tense and meaning unchanged.

title: Choosing a dress

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: I am looking for a dress for Clarice and Ethan’s wedding.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.text: The assistant said the red one was available in your size.

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: Did she say whether I could try it on?

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.text: Yes. She said the fitting room was free.

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: I like it. Clarice told me the celebration would be in the afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.text: Then it sounds suitable. Let’s check the invitation before we choose accessories.

reading: In early September, Taylor and Sara look for a dress for the wedding on September nineteenth. Sara reports what the shop assistant said: the red dress was available in Taylor’s size, and the fitting room was free. Taylor remembers that Clarice said the celebration would be in the afternoon. Before choosing accessories, they check the invitation. The reported information supports a real decision in the continuing story.

questions.prompt: What event is Taylor shopping for?
What did the assistant say about the fitting room?

task: Report three statements and one question from the shop conversation. Adjust pronouns and tense where the context requires it.

title: A realistic plan

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: The dress is almost ready, but I keep comparing my plans with pictures online.

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: What still needs to be done before next week?

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: The final fitting is on September fifteenth. The florist will deliver on September eighteenth.

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: Then write those appointments down and set a time to stop scrolling.

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: You are right. The pictures do not show every difficulty behind a celebration.

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: We can help with the remaining tasks. You do not have to organize everything alone.

reading: One week before the wedding, Clarice feels distracted by idealized celebrations online. Taylor helps her focus on concrete tasks. The final dress fitting is on September fifteenth, and the florist will deliver on September eighteenth, before the wedding on September nineteenth. Clarice writes the appointments down and decides to limit her scrolling time. She also accepts help from her friends. The conversation connects planning, online information and everyday wellbeing without changing the wedding timeline.

questions.prompt: When does this episode take place?
Who will deliver on September eighteenth?
What does Clarice decide to limit?

focus: Content discussion: media and everyday decisions
task: Discuss how online images can influence expectations. Support your opinion with one event from the story and one clearly labeled personal example.

title: People who inspire us

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.text: I am preparing a short speech about people who inspire me.

dialogue.speaker: Denali
dialogue.text: What would you like your audience to remember?

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.text: That achievements often depend on support. Clarice built her design work with help from friends.

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: And you have worked hard on your school projects. Give specific examples, not just compliments.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.text: I will also research a writer for my class, using reliable sources.

dialogue.speaker: Denali
dialogue.text: Good. Separate what you know from what you still need to verify.

reading: During the final wedding preparations, Sara works on a speech about people who inspire her. Denali encourages her to identify a clear message. Sara chooses the importance of support and uses Clarice’s design work as an example. Clarice asks her to use specific evidence. Sara also plans to research a writer for class, but she has not selected one yet. The friends distinguish verified information from ideas that still need research.

questions.prompt: Whose design work does she mention?
Has Sara selected a writer yet?

task: Choose a person who has contributed to a community. Separate facts, opinions and unanswered research questions.

title: A celebration with less waste

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.text: Everything is ready for our small celebration tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: I have brought reusable plates, so we will not need disposable ones.

dialogue.speaker: Denali
dialogue.text: We should also plan portions and save the untouched food safely.

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: Thank you. I wanted a relaxed evening with friends before tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.text: Small decisions will not solve every global problem, but they can reduce waste here.

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: Exactly. Let’s enjoy the evening and leave the room as tidy as we found it.

reading: On the evening before the wedding, Clarice celebrates with Taylor, Denali and Maria. They choose a small gathering. Taylor brings reusable plates, and the friends plan portions to reduce food waste. Maria points out that these choices do not solve every global problem, but they can make a practical difference at their own event. Clarice enjoys a relaxed evening before the wedding the next day. The episode links a personal celebration to a wider discussion about resources.

questions.prompt: What does Maria say about their choices?

focus: Content discussion: future challenges and resources
task: Propose three practical changes for an event. Explain their benefits and limits without making unsupported claims.

title: The day has arrived

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.text: The guests are here, and my speech is ready. I have butterflies in my stomach.

dialogue.speaker: Denali
dialogue.text: That means you are nervous. Take your time; everyone is glad to hear you.

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: The ceremony is about to begin. Thank you all for helping us get here.

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: From a pair of lost keys to this day! What a journey.

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.text: After the ceremony, let’s take a photograph with all our friends.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.text: And this time, I know exactly what to say: congratulations!

reading: On September nineteenth, Clarice and Ethan celebrate their wedding with their friends. Sara is ready to give her speech but says she has butterflies in her stomach, an idiom meaning that she feels nervous. Denali reassures her. Clarice remembers the keys Ethan returned when they first met. After the ceremony, the group plans a photograph. The story closes by connecting the first meeting, the friendships and the preparations to a celebration that finally takes place.

questions.prompt: What does butterflies in my stomach mean here?
What do they plan after the ceremony?

task: Explain an idiom in plain English. Compare two ways of congratulating someone, noting context and tone rather than stereotypes.
